grades.reason: Explains that swtch saves and restores a process's registers into p->context (a kernel thread context). It also notes forkret is set as the context ra for a new process. It does not list which registers swtch saves, and it does not compare them with the user trapframe.

grades.quote: kernelvec pushes all 32 registers onto the current stack, from which it will later restore them so that the interrupted kernel code can resume without disturbance.
grades.reason: Describes traps from kernel space. kernelvec pushes all 32 registers onto the interrupted kernel thread's stack, which contrasts with the user trapframe. It does not cover swtch's saved context or the user trapframe itself, so it is only auxiliary.

grades.quote: The kernel allocates, for each process, a page of memory for a trapframe structure that (among other things) has space to save the 32 user registers (1992).
grades.reason: Covers the user-trap side. uservec saves all 32 user registers into a per-process trapframe page, using sscratch and a0. This is the trapframe half of the comparison. It does not discuss swtch or the context it saves.
